title: Pinoresinol diglucoside from Eucommia ulmoides attenuates diabetic cardiomyopathy through suppressing the store-operated calcium entry and downregulating the STIM1/Orai1/NFAT3 signaling pathway.
authors: Feng, Yujie; Mao, Yanan; Li, Junshuai; Sun, Zhipeng; Wang, Yingchao; Wang, Xinru; Wang, Feng; Liu, Tiantian; Zhang, Lane
one_liner_zh: 该文研究中药成分PDG对糖尿病心肌病的保护作用，涉及分子对接但核心是细胞信号通路与动物实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系或结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Pinoresinol diglucoside (PDG), an active component derived from Eucommia ulmoides, exhibits therapeutic effects against apoptosis, inflammation, and hypertrophy, etc. However, whether PDG plays a protective role in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is not fully elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the role and potential mechanism of PDG in DCM. The possible mechanism of PDG targeting DCM was identified by network pharmacology, bioinformatics, machine learning and molecular docking methods. The heart function of mice was evaluated using echocardiography. The pathological changes in the heart of mice were detected using H&E staining. Changes of Ca(2+) fluorescence intensity values in H9c2 cells were assessed by confocal microscopy. Apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining and flow cytometry. The expression of DCM-related genes and proteins, both in vivo and in vitro, was examined by qRT-PCR and Western blot. The results showed that PDG effectively improved the cardiac function and suppressed cardiac hypertrophy, inflammation, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis caused by DCM. Intriguingly, molecular docking results revealed that the therapeutic effect of PDG on DCM was associated with stromal interaction molecule 1 (STIM1), calcium release-activated calcium channel protein 1 (Orai1), and nuclear factor of activated T-cells 3 (NFAT3) signaling. Consistently, animal experiments results indicated that PDG significantly downregulated the expression of STIM1, Orai1, NFAT3 at the protein level, as well as the associated store-operated calcium entry (SOCE). Therefore, our findings revealed that PDG can alleviate cardiac hypertrophy, inflammation and apoptosis in DCM by downregulating the STIM1, Orai1, and NFAT3 signaling molecules. Thus, PDG may be a promising therapeutic candidate for treating DCM.
abstract_zh: 松脂醇二葡萄糖苷（PDG）是从杜仲（Eucommia ulmoides）中提取的一种活性成分，对细胞凋亡、炎症和肥大等具有治疗作用。然而，PDG在糖尿病心肌病（DCM）中是否发挥保护作用尚未完全阐明。本研究旨在探讨PDG在DCM中的作用及其潜在机制。通过网络药理学、生物信息学、机器学习和分子对接方法确定了PDG靶向DCM的可能机制。使用超声心动图评估小鼠的心脏功能。通过H&E染色检测小鼠心脏的病理变化。通过共聚焦显微镜评估H9c2细胞中Ca(2+)荧光强度值的变化。通过TUNEL染色和流式细胞术评估细胞凋亡。通过qRT-PCR和Western blot检测体内外DCM相关基因和蛋白的表达。结果表明，PDG有效改善了心脏功能，并抑制了DCM引起的心脏肥大、炎症和心肌细胞凋亡。有趣的是，分子对接结果显示，PDG对DCM的治疗作用与基质相互作用分子1（STIM1）、钙释放激活钙通道蛋白1（Orai1）和活化T细胞核因子3（NFAT3）信号相关。一致地，动物实验结果表明，PDG在蛋白水平上显著下调了STIM1、Orai1、NFAT3的表达，以及相关的钙库操纵性钙内流（SOCE）。因此，我们的发现揭示，PDG通过下调STIM1、Orai1和NFAT3信号分子，可减轻DCM中的心脏肥大、炎症和细胞凋亡。因此，PDG可能是治疗DCM的有前景的候选药物。
